newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER IN FRIDAY TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER IN FRIDAY TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market edged further up on Friday from where they last closed on Wednesday, dealers said.
"The market is still firming and the central bank is continually accepting higher bids (at its treasury bill auctions)," one dealer said.

Market analysts say the rates have been on steady upward trend in the last couple of weeks because players felt previous rates of around 16 percent were too low given the current inflation levels of 19.9 percent.
On Friday, the Reserve Bank auctioned Z$249 million worth of treasury bills with an average yield of 19 percent, up from the previous 18.11 percent.
Discount houses were selling treasury bills on the secondary market at 17.5 percent from 17 percent but call money held steady at 17 percent.

Bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 19 percent from 18.25 (buying) and unchanged at 17.50 percent (selling) while 30-, 60- and 90-day NCDs firmed to 20 and 18.70 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 18 percent and 17.75 percent.
Reserve Bank figures showed the market closed on Wednesday with a Z$181 million surplus, up from Tuesday's Z$127 million.
